CP_s1.explanation: The unit responds to upright, side-on views of the body or flank of four-legged animals, mostly dogs (plus one weasel), and separately to the side of cars and trucks at wheel and door level. Both depend on a horizontal body above ground-contact legs or wheels.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to upright, side-on views of the body or flank of four-legged animals, mostly dogs (plus one weasel), and separately to the side of cars and trucks at wheel and door level. Both depend on a horizontal body above ground-contact legs or wheels.
parsed.evidence: In the top 20, 12 photos are side-on dogs or animals and 8 are side-on vehicles, all with the box on the mid-body. The unit loses almost everything under rotate_90 (3%, percentile 0), patch shuffling (24%, percentile 0) and rotate_180 (38%), but is fully mirror-invariant (101%), so it codes an upright horizontal object layout rather than texture or colour.
parsed.missing_data: Activations for side-on vehicles and animals outside the top 20, such as horses, cows, buses and trains, plus front-on views of cars and dogs, would show whether this is one 'horizontal elongated body on legs or wheels' shape feature or two separate detectors.

CP_s2.explanation: The unit responds to the side-on profile of an upright, horizontally elongated body held up by supports underneath, such as a standing dog's flank over its legs or a car's body over its wheels. It appears to encode this configural shape rather than any object category.

parsed.explanation: The unit responds to the side-on profile of an upright, horizontally elongated body held up by supports underneath, such as a standing dog's flank over its legs or a car's body over its wheels. It appears to encode this configural shape rather than any object category.
parsed.evidence: The top 20 mix side-view standing dogs (and a weasel) with side-view cars and vans at similar activations (7-10), and the boxes sit on the body mass just above the legs or wheels; random photos, including close-up dog heads and a non-standing dog, stay at 0-3. The unit keeps little activation under rotate_90 (3%), patch shuffling (24%) and rotate_180 (38%), all at very low percentiles, yet is fully mirror-invariant (101%) and largely colour-invariant, which fits an upright, left-right-symmetric global shape detector.
parsed.missing_data: Activations on non-dog side-view quadrupeds (horses, cattle) and other wheeled vehicles, plus front-view dogs and cars, would show whether this is a generic side-profile shape detector or two separate dog and car detectors.
